description: The AMS sign-in page, captured by the example pipeline step referenced in "How to regenerate screenshots" below.
The Wagtail CMS dashboard immediately after signing in as the sample admin account, captured by the example pipeline step.
The AMS sign-in page, before entering any credentials.
The page you land on immediately after signing in, showing the Staff links section with the Website Admin and Wagtail CMS buttons.
The Wagtail CMS dashboard, reached via the Wagtail CMS button.
The Django admin index, reached via the Website Admin button.
The Association settings page before the association name has been set.
The confirmation message after saving the association's short and long name.
The image chooser's Upload tab, open and empty, reached from the Association logo field.
The uploaded logo now selected in the Association logo field, before the form is saved.
The confirmation message after saving the logo with both navbar and footer toggles on.
The public homepage showing the logo in the navbar and footer.
Theme Settings scrolled to the Primary colour section, showing the default blue.
The Primary field now showing a purple brand colour after saving.
The Sans-serif font stack field now showing a different font after saving.
The home page's edit form, before any content has been added to its Body.
A Title block added to the home page's Body as its main heading, saved as a draft.
A Lead paragraph tagline added under the Title block, saved as a draft.
The preview panel showing the title and tagline as they will appear on the live site, before publishing.
The confirmation message after publishing the home page.
The page type chooser shown after clicking Add child page under Home.
The new About page with its title and a Paragraph block filled in, saved as a draft.
The confirmation message after publishing the About page, shown on the home page's child page list.
The new Contact page with a Contact Form block added and its recipient email filled in, saved as a draft.
The published Contact page on the live site, showing the contact form visitors see.
The Main menu editor for the English site, before any menu items have been added.
A menu item linked to the About page, chosen but not yet saved.
Both the About and Contact menu items filled in, not yet saved.
The confirmation message after saving the menu with About and Contact added.
The public site showing About and Contact in the navigation menu.
The confirmation message after publishing a new "Our story" page under About, shown on About's own child page list.
The public site with the About menu item expanded, showing Our story as a dropdown item, added automatically because About now has a published child page.
The confirmation message after moving Contact above About in the menu editor and saving.
The empty Add flat menu form.
The Add flat menu form filled in with a title, site, handle, and heading, not yet saved.
A footer menu item linked to the About page, not yet saved.
A footer menu item linking to an external website via a custom URL and custom link text, not yet saved.
The confirmation message after saving the footer column, listed among the site's flat menus.
The public site's footer showing two independently named columns, each with its own heading and links.
The public site's language switcher open, as seen by a signed-out visitor, listing Te Reo Māori and English.
The Te Reo Māori home page, reached via the language switcher, still empty because no content has been added to it yet.
The Pages explorer at the root level, showing a separate Home page for each enabled language.
The page type chooser shown after clicking Add child page under the Te Reo Māori Home.
The new Māori About page's Promote tab, with its title and content already filled in and its slug corrected to match the English About page's web address.
The confirmation message after publishing the Māori About page.
The Māori About page, reached directly from the English About page by clicking the language switcher, proving the two matching web addresses line up.
The empty Add membership option form in the Django admin.
The new Standard membership option listed after saving, in the Django admin.
The membership application page, showing the new membership option as a pricing card, exactly as a member sees it.
The account page after applying, showing the pending-review message and the new membership's Pending status and awaiting-payment invoice.
The pending membership's admin record, showing Status: Pending and an empty Approved datetime field.
The same admin record after filling in Approved datetime and saving, now showing Status: Active.
The rendered HTML content of the staff notification email sent when the application was submitted.
The empty Add profile field group form in the Django admin.
The new Teaching details group listed after saving, in the Django admin.
The empty Add profile field form in the Django admin.
The new teaching_subject field listed after saving, in the Django admin.
The account page's profile-completion nudge, showing 1 profile field remaining and a Complete your profile link.
The account update form, scrolled to the new Teaching details group, showing its Recommended and Required for membership badges.
The account page after answering the field and saving, with the profile-completion nudge no longer showing.
The AMS sign-in page, reached by visiting the forum's own address before signing in to the website.
The forum's home page, signed in as the site admin, with the Admin link visible in the sidebar.
The forum's Categories page, showing the three starter categories: General, Site Feedback, and Staff.
The empty New category form, not submitted.
A member's account page, showing the "you must have an active membership" message after trying to visit the forum without one.
The empty Add location form.
The new location listed after saving.
The empty Add event form.
The new event listed after saving, showing Published: False.
The event's admin record after checking Published and saving.
The public events page, showing the published event in Upcoming Events and on the map.
The event's own public page, showing its details and the Register to attend event button.
The empty Add resource form.
The new resource listed after saving, showing Published: False.
The resource's admin record after checking Published and saving.
The public resources page, showing the published resource listed.
The resource's own public page, showing its description, component, and author.
The empty Add user form in the Django admin.
The new user's Change user page, reached automatically after saving the Add user form.
The Permissions fieldset after ticking Staff status and adding Editors under Groups, then saving.
The confirmation email a new team member receives before they can sign in.
The new team member's own account page, showing the Staff links they now have access to.

The individual membership application form, cropped to the title, three pricing options, start date field, and submit button. Requires seed-marketing.sh, not seed.sh -- see docs-conventions.md's marketing screenshots section.
The account page's memberships table, cropped to the table itself, showing a past paid membership, a current paid membership, and a future membership awaiting payment. Requires seed-marketing.sh.

The About page's editor, populated with real About-page content (Title, Lead paragraph, Paragraph blocks) rather than example content, scrolled past the Visibility/Is structure only fields. Requires seed-marketing.sh.

The Discourse homepage, signed in via SSO (this Discourse instance requires it, no signed-out view is possible), showing several topics with replies from multiple demo accounts. Requires seed-marketing.sh and its Discourse fixture script -- see the permanent-content note in docs-conventions.md.

The public events page's own main content, signed out and cropped to exclude the header/breadcrumbs/footer, showing multiple events and map pins spread across several NZ regions. Requires seed-marketing.sh.
The public resources page's own main content, signed out and cropped to the first 4 resource cards, excluding the header/breadcrumbs/footer. Requires seed-marketing.sh.

Three navbar crops stacked into one composite image, each a different fictional association with its own menu items, theme, and Theme Settings configuration: the first has a wordmark logo coloured to match its navbar; the second has an emoji in its name, renamed About/Events links, no Forum link, and no language picker; the third has a gradient background, an SVG logo, no Resources link, a Forum link renamed to Community. Requires seed-marketing.sh.
